title: Saaty job selection example - three published matrices
description: Three pairwise comparison matrices from the job-choice example in Saaty's 2008 overview paper, each published together with its priority vector: the five main criteria with respect to the goal (Table 3), the subcriteria of Flexibility (Table 4), and the four job alternatives with respect to potential increase in salary (Table 5). The source publishes priorities but not consistency figures for these matrices, so lambda_max, CI and CR are derived here. The paper's remaining matrices for this example are not published and are not included.

source.citation: T. L. Saaty, 'Decision making with the analytic hierarchy process', International Journal of Services Sciences 1(1), 2008, pp. 83-98; Tables 3-5, pp. 88.

scale.name: saaty-1-9
scale.notes: Judgments on Saaty's fundamental 1-9 scale; reciprocals (e.g. 1/3) and intermediate or fractional values are valid entries. Matrix entries may be given as numbers or as fraction strings such as "1/3".

ri_table.name: saaty
ri_table.source: T. L. Saaty, The Analytic Hierarchy Process, McGraw-Hill, 1980. Values as tabulated in J. A. Alonso and M. T. Lamata, 'Consistency in the analytic hierarchy process: a new approach', International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems 14(4), 2006, Table 1 (Wharton column).

matrices.description: Table 3: main criteria with respect to the goal.
Table 4: subcriteria with respect to Flexibility.
Table 5: alternatives with respect to potential increase in salary.

provenance.method: Principal right eigenvector of the pairwise comparison matrix (computed with numpy.linalg.eig; the Perron root is lambda_max), normalized to sum to 1. CI = (lambda_max - n)/(n - 1); CR = CI / RI(n) for the RI table declared in this fixture. Reproduce with tools/compute_expected.py.

Column-normalization mean (Saaty's approximate method): normalize each column of the matrix to sum to 1, then average across columns; lambda_max is estimated as the mean of (A*w)_i / w_i. This is the prioritization method implemented by, among others, the npm 'ahp' package. Reproduce with tools/compute_expected.py.
